artifacts.summary: Implementation summary covering all three phases: worked example/probe landed, plan-authoring keyword added, redeploy verified end to end.

completion_data.completion_summary: Landed the rw-site definitional-unfold worked example and an enumerated, runnable twelve-spelling grep probe in dependency-tracing.md, tagged the file's own index entry with the plan-authoring keyword to make it reachable at plan time, and verified end to end after redeploy that the Stage 4 item 13 query now selects the file for a lean4 plan dispatch.

memory_candidates.content: When resyncing an index-entries.json entry's line_count field after editing its referenced markdown file, anchor the Edit's old_string on the entry's "path" + "line_count" line pair together, not a bare "line_count": N -- the bare value is frequently non-unique across a multi-entry index file and the Edit tool will refuse an ambiguous match.

deploy-headless.sh's internal verify-deploy.sh fast-gate sweep can transiently FAIL (e.g. 3 of 41 checks) during a sibling task's in-flight, not-yet-committed edit under a concurrent multi-task /orchestrate batch -- observed as doc-lint content-drift on the sibling's own uncommitted files plus a load-correlated gate6 timeout (explicitly flagged CONTENTION in gate6's own output). Re-running deploy-headless.sh after the sibling's commit lands is the correct recovery, not treating the red as this task's own regression -- check git log/status for the specific failing paths against your own declared file_scope before escalating.

sapience_notes.subject: planner-agent.md Stage 4 item 13 context-discovery gate
sapience_notes.value: Plan-time discovery of project/** context content runs through exactly one mechanism: planner-agent.md Stage 4 item 13, gated on load_when.task_types[] matching the dispatch's task_type AND keywords[]/topics[] containing the literal string plan-authoring. The task_types axis alone is necessary but not sufficient; load_when.agents[] plays no part in this gate.

sapience_notes.subject: Cross-domain-shared-agent hazard in index-entries.json load_when.agents[]
sapience_notes.value: Naming a cross-domain shared agent (e.g. planner-agent) inside a domain-specific index entry's load_when.agents[] is mechanically prohibited: planner-agent.md itself carries an explicit MUST NOT, and context-discovery.md names this exact scenario as the Cross-Domain-Shared-Agent Hazard -- doing so would pull that domain's content into every other domain's plan dispatch.

sapience_notes.subject: deploy-headless.sh verify-deploy fast-gate transient failures under concurrent batch dispatch
sapience_notes.value: During a multi-task /orchestrate batch, deploy-headless.sh's internal verify-deploy.sh pass can transiently report FAIL (e.g. 3 of 41 checks) purely from a concurrent sibling task's in-flight, uncommitted edit to its own declared files plus load-correlated gate timeouts (gate6 explicitly self-flags CONTENTION when entry-vs-kill-time load ratio exceeds 2.0). Re-running after the sibling commits clears it to a clean 41/41 pass with no source change on the observing task's side.

sapience_notes.subject: index-entries.json line_count coupling
sapience_notes.value: Every indexed context file's entry in index-entries.json carries a line_count field that must track that file's actual wc -l; deploy-headless.sh runs a generate-context-line-counts.sh --write sweep that auto-repairs drift across every extension's source index on each deploy, so an uncorrected manual edit is only ever transiently out of sync, not permanently.

sapience_notes.subject: dependency-tracing.md Grep-Based Blast Radius section's pre-existing state
sapience_notes.value: The generic rw-site definitional-unfold caveat (grep importers under-counts blast radius; must also grep unfold spellings) was already present in dependency-tracing.md before this task, landed independently by an unrelated cross-repository conclusion-stage dispatch deriving from the identical issue-log entry. The actual gap closed by this task was narrower: a concrete worked example, an enumerated runnable multi-spelling probe, and the file's plan-time reachability (missing plan-authoring keyword) -- not the caveat's substantive absence.

sapience_notes.subject: git-commit-phase.sh completeness check under concurrent git index.lock contention
sapience_notes.value: Under a multi-task /orchestrate batch sharing one working tree, a git-commit-phase.sh invocation can hit a transient git index.lock contention from a concurrent sibling's own commit, causing the wrapper's own retry-after-backoff to still leave the completeness check failing (exit 6) because the staged content never actually committed. The correct recovery is to re-run the identical git-commit-phase.sh invocation once the lock clears, never widen the pathspec or fall back to a raw git commit.
